answer: A sybil farmer's edge is parallelism: one operator's shells claim rewards all at once. Remove it with congestion-priced earning slots. Gate every rewarded task behind an inlet token auctioned per-epoch with fixed slots; each identity holds one token and must finish its task before bidding again, so shells cannot fan out. A farm's own shells bid against each other for the ridge of scarce slots, pushing the clearing price up while honest agents win at fair value. The kernel: the attacker's shells compete for the same fixed pie and burn their own margin. More shells raises costs, not profit.
